summary:
LUNA-VISTA is an interactive, science-based web application designed to assist mission planners, researchers, educators, and the public in identifying and comparing suitable landing locations near the Moon's south pole. The system combines astronomical calculations, lunar terrain analysis, and 3D visualization to simplify the evaluation of potential lunar landing sites.

The application allows users to select different candidate landing locations and mission dates to analyze the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon. Using NASA/JPL SPICE data and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) terrain datasets, it calculates solar elevation, sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and potential direct-to-Earth communication windows. It also estimates solar energy generation based on illumination conditions and solar panel parameters.

An intelligent site comparison and recommendation module evaluates candidate locations using sunlight availability, communication visibility, and terrain suitability. The results are presented through interactive 3D lunar visualizations, graphs, comparative dashboards, and mission reports.

The main goal of LUNA-VISTA is to provide a user-friendly scientific decision-support platform that makes complex lunar environmental data easier to understand, helping users evaluate landing sites and mission dates for safer and more efficient future lunar exploration.
details:
LUNA-VISTA: Intelligent Lunar Landing Site Selection and Mission Planning System

LUNA-VISTA is a proposed lunar exploration planning system designed to help identify and compare suitable landing sites near the Moon's South Pole. It focuses on three important factors: sunlight availability, Earth visibility for communication, and local terrain conditions.

The system allows users to select candidate landing sites and dates. It then aims to analyze the positions of the Sun and Earth, examine terrain obstructions, estimate sunlight duration and communication windows, and compare different landing locations. Based on these factors, it provides an explainable ranking of candidate sites using configurable criteria.

The project is designed around scientific datasets, including NASA/JPL SPICE kernels for planetary positions and orientations, LOLA elevation models for lunar terrain analysis, and LROC imagery for surface visualization.

The main benefits of LUNA-VISTA are improved mission-planning support, easier comparison of landing locations, better understanding of lighting and communication constraints, and more accessible visualization of complex lunar environment information. Its intended impact is to support safer and more informed planning for future lunar exploration missions.

The creative aspect of this project is its combination of solar analysis, Earth visibility assessment, terrain evaluation, and site comparison in one integrated and user-friendly concept. It also emphasizes transparency by showing the criteria behind its recommendations.

This submission presents a concept demonstration. The sample site scores and comparison values shown in the presentation are illustrative mock data, not actual measured lunar results or official NASA rankings. The proposed system would require implementation and scientific validation using the relevant datasets.
